root_cause.text: `sev_ioctl_do_pdh_export()` in the CCP/SEV driver copied the firmware-reported PDH certificate lengths and user buffers to userspace even when `__sev_do_cmd_locked()` had failed, so a PSP length error could make `copy_to_user()` read past the kernel-allocated blob and leak memory.
root_cause.evidence: The patch adds `if (ret || WARN_ON_ONCE(argp->error)) goto e_free_cert;` before any `copy_to_user()`, and the CVE text says “don’t attempt to copy the blobs to userspace if the firmware command failed” because on an invalid-length failure “copying the number of bytes _firmware_ requires will overflow the kernel-allocated buffer and leak data to userspace.”

intent_record.intent_summary: Clarify the firmware length-handling comment for PDH export response processing.
intent_record.what: The comment above the assignments to `input.cert_chain_len` and `input.pdh_cert_len` was replaced with a longer multi-line comment explaining that firmware returns blob lengths, either the minimum required length or the actual written length, and that these values should be returned to userspace.
intent_record.how: This change does not alter runtime behavior; it clarifies the meaning of the length values returned from firmware and documents why they are copied back to the user-facing structure.

intent_record.intent_summary: Add an error check after PDH export to abort and clean up on failed or invalid export results.
intent_record.what: A new conditional check was inserted after the certificate export call: `if (ret || WARN_ON_ONCE(argp->error)) goto e_free_cert;`. This adds an early exit before the `pdh_blob` copy-to-user block when the previous operation failed or when `argp->error` is set.
intent_record.how: At runtime, the function now stops processing and frees the certificate buffer if the export step returned an error or unexpectedly left `argp->error` set. This prevents continuing into the user-copy path with an invalid or failed export result, avoiding propagation of a bad PDH export state.

The change adds error handling after PDH export so failed/invalid export results are detected and aborted instead of being copied to userspace, which directly addresses the root cause where an error path could leak memory.

candidates.rationale: This branch allows the code to proceed with exporting the PDH blob without first verifying that the firmware command succeeded or that the blob/length is valid, which is the condition that led to copying stale or oversized data to userspace.

This is the userspace copy operation that can leak memory if the earlier firmware-reported length is invalid after a failed __sev_do_cmd_locked() call, causing copy_to_user() to read past the allocated kernel buffer.
The length passed here comes from the firmware-reported PDH certificate length; if that length is wrong after a PSP error, this statement drives the out-of-bounds read into userspace.

vuln_statements.explanation: This branch allowed the code to continue toward userspace export even when the preceding firmware command could have failed, enabling later use of an invalid or oversized PDH blob.

bic_trace_step.reason: The shown commit introduces `sev_ioctl_do_pdh_export()`-style export logic that copies PSP-reported lengths and buffers to userspace after issuing the SEV command, and there is no error-gating that would stop use of the returned lengths on command failure. The vulnerable pattern is present: the code relies on firmware-reported certificate sizes and then performs user copies from the kernel blob without checking that `__sev_do_cmd_locked()` succeeded. Because this is the initial implementation commit, the fix is not present here. In other words, the snippet contains the susceptible construct described in the root cause: copying the PDH/certificate-chain data to userspace using firmware-provided lengths even when the underlying SEV command may have failed, which can lead to `copy_to_user()` reading beyond the allocated blob.
